clue.text: Wise bookmaker briefly in charge promises to pay

indicators.note: briefly says the name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Jude is the writer of the biblical Epistle of Jude, so a maker of a book
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A sensible turf accountant, for a short while in charge, writes IOUs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' suggests a betting shop, but here it is the author of a book of the Bible; 'briefly' drops the E of JUDE to leave JUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Judicious describes sound judgement, a straightforward synonym of being sensible and prudent.

clue.text: Frenchman getting pence for his last drink

indicators.note: the coin replaces the final letter of the Frenchman's name

parts.note: Jules is a typical French man's name
P is the abbreviation for pence in British money

explanation.surface: A Frenchman pays a few coins for his final drink of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting pence for his last' means P takes the place of the last letter, S, of JULES.
explanation.definitionFit: A julep is a sweet drink, most famously the bourbon-and-mint cocktail of the American South.

clue.text: Craft with piece in board game yielding ability to draw

parts.note: in British English a draughtsman is a counter in the game of draughts (checkers)
a ship is a sea-going craft

explanation.surface: Skill with a counter in a board game produces a talent for sketching.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers, and its pieces are called draughtsmen; 'Craft' looks like skill but is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughtsmanship is skill at drawing, especially technical or artistic drawing.

clue.text: Primitive work of art that's a liquid asset

parts.note: crude means rough, primitive, unrefined
an oil is a painting done in oil paints

explanation.surface: A naive painting turns out to be worth cashing in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid asset' usually means cash, but here it is literally a valuable liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrefined petroleum is a valuable commodity that is literally a fluid, a punning take on ready money.

clue.text: Orchestral, piece written on back of envelope, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A score for the orchestra jotted down on the back of an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orchestral piece' reads as a composition, but it is an instrument, a piece of the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodwind instrument is a standard member of a symphony orchestra, so an orchestral piece of kit.

clue.text: Shades of ancient Chinese princesses?

parts.note: the Sung (Song) dynasty ruled China from the tenth to the thirteenth century
princesses are girls, or lasses; the query flags the playful equation

explanation.surface: Asks whose ghosts haunt the court of old Chinese royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shades' suggests ghosts but means dark glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades is informal for dark glasses worn against bright light.

clue.text: Intensity of short section, hard to follow

parts.note: Dept is the short form of department, a section of an organisation
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: How strong is a brief passage that is tough to keep up with?
explanation.definitionFit: Depth can mean intensity, as in the depth of a colour or of feeling.

clue.text: Information about ancient city's poisonous plant

indicators.note: about says the word for information surrounds the city

parts.note: data is information
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Records concerning an ancient city's deadly vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Datura is a genus of toxic flowering plants, including thorn apple and jimsonweed.

clue.text: Basic fare for one who regularly crosses the earth

definitions.text: Basic fare for one who regularly crosses the earth

parts.words: Basic fare for one who regularly crosses the earth
parts.note: read literally, the midday meal of a farm worker who drives his team across the soil, row after row

explanation.surface: Simple food for someone who keeps crossing the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly crosses the earth' suggests a world traveller, but means going up and down a field turning the soil; the answer is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: This pub staple is a simple cold plate of bread, cheese and pickle, nominally a farm worker's midday food.

clue.text: Proverbial loser is switching into alternative theatre

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other
alternative signals a different arrangement of the letters of theatre
switching says the two letters of is swap round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A failure is moving into fringe drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching' turns IS into SI, which goes 'into' HETATER, an anagram of THEATRE signalled by 'alternative'. The proverb is 'He who hesitates is lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says one who delays is lost, so such a dithering person is the proverbial loser.

clue.text: Pacific group about to enter long-distance races

parts.note: a league is an old measure of a long distance, about three miles
of can mean about or concerning, as in 'speak of'
nations are peoples or races

explanation.surface: A team from the Pacific coast takes part in marathons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts OF between the other two pieces. 'Pacific' suggests the ocean but means peace-making.
explanation.definitionFit: The interwar international body was founded to keep peace, so it was a peaceable, pacific group of states.

clue.text: Silver piece's replacement — first penny, say, then pound, say

parts.note: eg (for example) is signalled by 'say'
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
eg again, for example

explanation.surface: A coin's substitute: first a penny, perhaps, then a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver' is Long John Silver of Treasure Island, not the metal; his missing leg was replaced by a wooden one.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver had a wooden leg, which replaced the limb he lost.

clue.text: Perfect exam performance, or just fair

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means acceptable or so-so, and read literally describes a paper with every answer correct.

clue.text: Getting to the top immediately and honestly!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation meaning truly, no kidding

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means vertically upwards and is also slang for frankly or without exaggeration.

clue.text: Section of group at riot is manifesting loyalty

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a crowd at a riot shows devotion to the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Patriotism is devotion and loyalty to one's own country.

clue.text: Left in pub, ales I ordered easy to swallow

indicators.note: ordered says the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Left in the pub, the ales I ordered went down nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like asking for drinks at the bar, but it is the anagram signal; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea easy to swallow is one easily believed, so credible.

clue.text: Drop out of old college

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Quit an old university.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop something, such as a name from a list, is to leave it out.

clue.text: Preserve one in a tin for islander

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve

indicators.note: in says the numeral goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a can is a tin
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Fruit conserve packed in a can for someone from the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Caribbean island of Jamaica.

clue.text: Host runs into a little woman

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the name

parts.note: Amy March is one of the four sisters in Little Women
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A host dashes into a small lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little woman' looks like a small lady but refers to Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large number, especially of soldiers, so a multitude or armed force.

clue.text: Person urging caution about crooked employee

indicators.note: about says the cautious person surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a warner is one who warns
agee (or ajee) is a dialect word for askew or crooked

explanation.surface: Someone cautioning against a dishonest member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: AGEE is an old Scottish and northern word for awry, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on wages is an employee, paid by an employer.

clue.text: Poet in state capital, heard but not seen

indicators.note: heard but not seen says the word matches in sound but not spelling

parts.note: Sydney is the capital of the Australian state of New South Wales

explanation.surface: A poet in an Australian city is heard but never spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Philip Sidney was an Elizabethan poet, author of Astrophel and Stella.

clue.text: Diagnose disorder in Pacific port

indicators.note: disorder signals a jumbling of the letters

explanation.surface: A doctor identifies an illness in a coastal city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' reads as an illness, fitting 'Diagnose', but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Californian city is a major harbour on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Speed up

parts.note: go faster, as a horse breaking into its fastest pace

explanation.definitionFit: A horse's fastest gait, so to go at that pace is to speed along.

clue.text: Assume one's employed?

annotationWithheld.why: Assume one's employed? (5): POSIT is POST around I, but 'employed' must both supply POST and put I inside it, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Take a furtive look in both directions

indicators.note: in both directions says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Sneaking a glance left and right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in both directions' looks like glancing left and right, but says the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to look quickly and secretly.

clue.text: Privately responsible for acts, partly

definitions.meaning: stagehands working behind the backdrops share in staging a play's acts

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means out of public view, and literally describes stage crew working behind the sets.

clue.text: Dead man, in vain

annotationWithheld.why: Dead man, in vain (5): EMPTY fits 'in vain', but no parse of 'Dead man' gives the letters and a search found no fuller text; possibly an OCR misread

clue.text: Hopping mad about current temperature, extremely warm

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the electrical symbol
mad signals the letters of Hopping are scrambled

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Furious over the latest temperature reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' turns HOPPING into PIPNGHO, which goes 'about' I; T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Piping hot describes food served very hot, steaming.
